provenance.notes: Out family batch. Low ticket, constant repeat work: the kit leans on seasonal start-ups, blowouts, backflow tests and service plans, with prices sized to small repair jobs. No controller or valve brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Spring sprinkler start-up and autumn blowout booking
pageStructurePlus.contains: What a start-up includes, the winterisation blowout before the first freeze, booking windows by month, and what happens if pipes freeze full of water
pageStructurePlus.why: Two seasonal visits are the backbone of this trade. A page that books them online fills the route before the rush.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Broken or stuck heads, a zone that won't turn on, a valve that won't shut off, low pressure, geysers, soggy spots and a controller that resets itself
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners describe the symptom, not the part. A trouble guide gets the right repair booked with the right parts on the van.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Why the water utility requires a yearly backflow test, what the tester checks, filing the certificate, and repairs if the device fails
pageStructurePlus.why: Backflow letters arrive with a deadline. A clear page turns a confusing notice into a booked, recurring appointment.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Weather-based controllers, rain and soil sensors, drip conversion for beds, matched-precipitation nozzles, and checking for a local water rebate
pageStructurePlus.why: High water bills and watering limits bring upgrade buyers. Showing the options sells the bigger ticket in a low-ticket trade.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Monthly irrigation inspections for HOAs, office parks and churches, repair authorisation limits, wet-check reports, and seasonal schedule changes
pageStructurePlus.why: Contract work smooths out the season. Property managers look for a page that shows the irrigation company can handle multiple sites.

designDirections.name: Fix My Sprinklers
designDirections.bestFor: One-van irrigation repair techs who win on answering fast and showing up the same week
designDirections.headlineSample: Sprinkler repair in {City}, booked this week
designDirections.whyItFits: Teal reads as water and tangerine makes the call button pop, and the humanist type feels like a helpful tech, not a company.

designDirections.name: Season Route
designDirections.bestFor: Irrigation companies whose year runs on start-ups, blowouts and backflow tests booked by route
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's combo. Linen and brick keep the booking cards calm and readable, and slab headings give a small local outfit some weight.

designDirections.name: Managed Irrigation
designDirections.bestFor: Irrigation firms bidding HOA, office park and municipal maintenance contracts
designDirections.headlineSample: Irrigation management for {City} HOAs and properties
designDirections.whyItFits: Steel blue and a neutral grotesque read like a facilities proposal, which is how property managers compare irrigation contractors.

openers.line: Someone in {City} with a sprinkler head shooting water into the street searches for repair and finds {Business Name} with no site. They want to know you fix that and when you can come.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What that homeowner would find instead: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing links to Facebook, where the start-up schedule is a post from weeks ago. A homeowner wants to book a sprinkler start-up, not scroll for the date.
openers.hook: Tap the link and confirm it goes to Facebook. Note any seasonal schedule post.
openers.linkLine: A sprinkler site where people book the visit: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site still has a free-host banner and last year's blowout prices. In a trade that runs on repeat visits, an out-of-date page makes customers call someone else.
openers.hook: Open their site and look for old prices, an old year or a builder banner. Note which.

openers.line: On a phone your sprinkler site's phone number isn't tappable. People look for irrigation repair standing in a wet lawn.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note what fails. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your sprinkler site, working on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.angle: No way to book a blowout
openers.line: There's no way to book a sprinkler blowout or start-up online with {Business Name}. Most customers would pick a slot in a minute and leave the gate code.
openers.hook: Check listing, bios and any site for online booking. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Online booking for start-ups and blowouts: {demo-link}

openers.line: You post the satisfying stuff: a cracked lateral dug out and fixed, a valve box cleaned up. Those irrigation repairs would sell more as a trouble guide than as scattered posts.
openers.hook: Find two repair posts you can name by problem. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your sprinkler repairs, sorted by problem: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention a water bill that dropped after a leak fix and a tech who explained the controller. That's exactly what new irrigation customers want to read, and it stays on your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about the bill, a leak or the controller. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the sprinkler fixes they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Every autumn the blowout calls arrive in the same two weeks before the first freeze. A booking page fills the irrigation route in order instead of by whoever calls loudest.
openers.hook: Use from late August through October in freeze climates, or March for start-ups. Name the season.

openers.line: Sprinklers break on Saturday when the system runs and the owner is home to see it. A repair request form catches that call while the water's still running.
openers.hook: Call their number on a weekend. If it hits voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A sprinkler repair request that works on weekends: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring an irrigation tech. Good techs check whether the company looks organised before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the role and date.
openers.linkLine: An irrigation company site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your irrigation route covers several towns, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you come there. 'Sprinkler repair' plus the town is the search.
openers.hook: Find towns in their reviews or posts; use one at the edge of their route.
openers.linkLine: A sprinkler page for each town on the route: {demo-link}

openers.line: If your water district offers a rebate on smart controllers, that belongs on your irrigation page. It's the easiest upgrade a homeowner says yes to.
openers.hook: Check whether their water district has a controller or drip rebate. Only use this if one exists.

openers.line: Backflow tests need a certified tester, and many states license irrigation work. Showing your licence and tester certification on a page answers the utility letter's first question.
openers.hook: Check the state registry and any backflow tester list for a record. Never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, backflow certification and testing on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like a lot of your sprinkler customers have been with you for years. When they move or a neighbour asks, they need a page to send people to.
openers.hook: Look for reviews mentioning years of service or neighbours. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where the next sprinkler referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a tidy irrigation repair. Work like that is what a stranger needs to see before trusting you in their yard.
openers.hook: Pick their newest repair or install post and name it: problem, fix, town if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That sprinkler job, front and centre: {demo-link}

objections.objection: My customers just call me every year.
objections.handler: "They do, all in the same two weeks. Online booking lets them pick a slot and leave the gate code, and you build the irrigation route instead of answering the phone."

objections.objection: My jobs are too small to need a website.
objections.handler: "That's why it's priced for a small outfit. A couple of weeks of blowouts covers it, and the booking page takes the busywork off you."

objections.objection: I'm already full in the spring.
objections.handler: "Then the site helps you fill the shoulders: backflow tests, controller upgrades and HOA contracts that pay outside the rush."
"Great. Happy to hand over the booking layout and the trouble guide. If it stalls before blowout season, the offer stands."

objections.objection: I'm on a lead platform already.
objections.handler: "Shared sprinkler leads go to several companies and you pay for each. Your own site books your repeat customers without a fee."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: seasonal booking, a trouble guide, a backflow page and a few town pages."

bullets: Size the build to the trade: a few weeks of blowout revenue should cover it, so keep the starter lean.
Online booking for start-ups, blowouts and backflow tests is the core feature; price each booking type as a line.
A trouble guide earns repair searches all season; price it once and add symptoms over time.
Add the HOA and commercial page only for companies that want contract work.
Keep monthly products small; this owner thinks in visits worth a few hundred dollars.
Never pad the build with gallery pages; irrigation customers buy on availability and trust, not portfolios.

lineItems.description: Max with utility-specific deadlines and a lookup for past test certificates.
Max when it covers controllers, drip conversion and the local rebate process.
Max with sample wet-check reports, insurance details and a bid request form.
Max when each page lists route days and local water rules.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for sprinkler service
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each week a sprinkler repair or upgrade goes on your Maps profile with the town, and seasonal hours stay correct through blowout season."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after each irrigation visit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After every start-up or repair, the customer gets a text asking for a review. With this many visits a year, reviews pile up fast."

whatElseYouSell.name: Blowout and start-up reminder postcards
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A postcard to last year's customers with the blowout booking link lands before they think about calling anyone else."
whatElseYouSell.when: Late August for blowouts, February for start-ups.

whatElseYouSell.name: Van wrap and door hanger artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your van parks on a dozen streets a day. A wrap with the booking site and a door hanger for the neighbours turns each stop into the next sprinkler call."

whatElseYouSell.name: Water-bill season upgrade campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When summer water bills arrive, a campaign for smart controllers and drip conversion reaches the customers most likely to upgrade their irrigation."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in May, run in July and August.

whatElseYouSell.name: HOA board one-sheet
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page irrigation capability sheet for HOA boards and property managers, with your wet-check report sample."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if they want contract work.

withoutAI.whoPays: The lawn care company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The mowing crews on your customers' lawns spot broken heads every week. I'll build their site, and they'll send the sprinkler repairs to you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Mowers see the problems first and rarely fix irrigation. The referral flows naturally.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The supply branch where you buy heads and valves has every irrigation contractor in town on its books. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Suppliers have budgets and a contractor list that is your prospect list.

withoutAI.whoPays: The plumbing company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Plumbers get backflow and outdoor leak calls they don't want. Their site can send those to you, and you send indoor work back."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Overlap at the backflow device makes a natural two-way referral.

withoutAI.whoPays: The landscape company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every new garden needs drip lines. The landscape installer who subs that to you needs a site, and your intro gets it built."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Landscapers rely on irrigation subs and trust the one they use.

withoutAI.whoPays: The sod company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "New sod dies without a working sprinkler system. The sod crew you check systems for needs a site too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Sod and irrigation are sold to the same lawn in the same week.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "HOA managers juggle irrigation complaints from residents by email. A common-area request page with zone and location fixes that."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers have a budget for resident tools and the irrigation client already services their common areas.

withAI.route: Parts lookup assistant for the irrigation supply branch
withAI.pitchLine: "Contractors describe or picture a broken head or valve and the assistant suggests the matching part in stock at that branch."
withAI.whyItWorks: Wrong-part returns cost the branch time; contractors stay loyal to the one that makes it easy.

withAI.route: Property issue spotter for the lawn crew
withAI.pitchLine: "Mowing crews snap a broken sprinkler head on the route and the assistant sends the homeowner a repair offer from your partner."
withAI.whyItWorks: The lawn crew earns a referral fee or goodwill; the irrigation client gets repairs.

withAI.route: Backflow notice helper for the water utility
withAI.pitchLine: "Residents with a backflow test notice ask what it means. An assistant answers and lists certified testers, including your client."
withAI.whyItWorks: Utilities field thousands of confused calls; the irrigation client knows the questions.

withAI.pitchLine: "Residents report dry patches and broken heads with a picture; the assistant groups them by zone and sends one sprinkler work order."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers stop forwarding single complaints; the irrigation client gets organised tickets.

withAI.route: Drip design helper for landscape installers
withAI.pitchLine: "Landscapers guess at drip runs for new beds. Upload the bed layout and get a draft parts list and zone count to send the irrigation sub for a firm price."
withAI.whyItWorks: Faster quotes for the landscaper and a steady stream of drip installs for your client.

withAI.route: Sod watering coach for the sod crew
withAI.pitchLine: "New sod customers get watering guidance by text for the first weeks, and a sprinkler check offer if zones look dry."
withAI.whyItWorks: Fewer dead-sod complaints for the sod crew and repair work for the irrigation client.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for sprinkler repairs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Miss a call in a valve box and the caller gets a text asking for the address, which zone is broken and a picture of the head."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Online start-up, blowout and backflow booking
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers pick a sprinkler blowout slot on their street's route day and leave the gate code. You stop playing phone tag in October."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 1, before the next season. Needs their route days, service prices and capacity per day.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for irrigation visits
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each review gets a reply drafted that mentions the repair or the blowout, ready for your thumbs-up between stops."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Card-on-file billing after each visit
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The card on file gets charged when the irrigation visit is marked done, with a receipt listing the heads and valves replaced."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their payment account and parts price list.

softwareAI.name: Last-year customer rebooking sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every customer from last season gets their sprinkler start-up or blowout offer with one-tap booking, before the season opens."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs last season's customer list with addresses.

softwareAI.name: Sprinkler symptom picture triage
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers send a picture of the geyser or the soggy spot, and the tool suggests the likely part, so the van has it on board."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past repair pictures labelled with the part used. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Route planner for seasonal visits
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Booked start-ups and blowouts are grouped by street and ordered by drive time, so a tech does more irrigation visits per day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the booking system live and their tech start points.

softwareAI.name: Backflow certificate tracker and utility filing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every backflow test result is stored by address with its due date, and the certificate goes to the utility the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the utility's filing format and their tester details.

softwareAI.name: After-hours sprinkler repair line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers evening calls, tells them how to shut off the irrigation at the valve tonight, and books the repair."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs shut-off instructions and their calendar. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Sprinkler chatbot on watering schedules and rules
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'how long should zone three run' and 'what days can I water' from your guidance and the local rules, and books a check if needed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their schedule guidance and local watering rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Zone map per property
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each customer gets a sprinkler zone map with valve locations and head types, so any tech can fix it without hunting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs techs to sketch zones on their next visit.

softwareAI.name: Wet-check report generator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Techs tap through each zone, note issues and pictures, and the HOA or homeowner gets a tidy irrigation report with repair approvals."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their inspection checklist.

softwareAI.name: Freeze warning blowout alerts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When an early freeze is forecast, unbooked customers get a text to book their blowout before the pipes crack."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, before autumn. Needs the customer list and their service area.

softwareAI.name: Water bill savings explainer drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From the customer's controller settings and lawn size, it drafts a plain note on what a smart controller or drip conversion could change, for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their upgrade prices and typical settings. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with zone map and visit history
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers see their sprinkler zone map, past visits and next blowout date, and book repairs without calling."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs zone maps and booking in place.

softwareAI.name: Voice notes to repair invoice
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Say what you replaced at the end of the irrigation visit, and it drafts the invoice with parts and labour for you to send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their parts list and labour rates. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Parts usage and van restock list
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Parts logged on each visit build a restock list for the van, so nobody drives back for a valve diaphragm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a basic parts list and techs logging parts.

softwareAI.name: HOA monthly irrigation summary writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From the month's wet checks it drafts a short summary for the HOA board: zones fixed, water saved, approvals needed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, once they hold HOA contracts. Needs wet-check reports. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by visit type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether start-ups, blowouts, backflow tests or repairs actually pay best per hour once drive time and parts are in."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs a season of visits with times and parts.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for irrigation techs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants say whether they've repaired valves and controllers and have a licence, and you only call the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they hire. Needs must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Seasonal sprinkler booking for every irrigation outfit

routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Low price, obvious pain and the same workflow everywhere.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Contractor finder for an irrigation parts distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners searching for sprinkler repair could be sent to contractors who buy from your branches. A finder keeps them loyal to you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors want contractor loyalty and lack a homeowner channel.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your backflow notices tell residents to find a certified tester. A searchable tester directory with online submission cuts calls to your office."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Utilities run compliance programs and need cleaner submissions.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Members switch on start-up, blowout and backflow booking with a trouble guide, as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: A practical member perk that reaches many small irrigation firms.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Residents apply for the controller rebate, book an approved contractor and upload the install proof in one flow."

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies don't know how sprinkler companies book by route. License the irrigation template with booking already wired."

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every community you manage reports sprinkler problems in one place, with pictures and zones, routed to the contracted irrigation company."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: School and parks irrigation schedule board

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: An irrigation company in another metro
